sources.reason: All endpoints require authentication and current read access is pay-per-use.

oEmbed is an official rendering mechanism for known post URLs, not a historical post API or a license to analyze user content. X states that permission from the original creator may still be required.
Member data requires OAuth and post retrieval permission is restricted to approved applications.
Caption listing and download require OAuth and sufficient content-owner permission.

First-party event metadata identifies speakers, but no speaker-attributed transcript is exposed for automatic ingestion. Databricks terms prohibit scraper, crawler, automated acquisition, data-mining, and systematic database collection, so these pages are never scraped.

The Ali Ghodsi transcript is downloadable, but its interviewer and speaker turns require verified segmentation. An older STVP article links a Creative Commons license that now returns 404; current Stanford terms limit downloads to personal, non-commercial use, so the transcript is not admitted without written or machine-verifiable license confirmation.

The Matei Zaharia transcript has explicit speaker labels and a public download, but ACM restricts copying and automated collection and requires permission for republication or redistribution. It remains catalog-only until the operator records permission for analytical use.
First-party identity and publication discovery; multi-author papers must not be treated as social voice.
The public API is admissible, but Databricks is private and does not provide public-company earnings-call filings for these leaders.
The production import path for lawfully obtained post exports and speaker-attributed transcripts; every item must match a reviewed catalog entry.
